prompt: You double a ripple adder's width while keeping the same per-stage delay model. What happens to the worst-case carry dependence?

options.text: It disappears because the new bit slices run in parallel
options.explanation: Upper stages still depend on the carry arriving from lower stages.

options.text: It spans twice as many serial stages
options.explanation: Correct. Widening adds dependent stages to the longest carry route.

options.text: It gains just one tree level
options.explanation: That describes a binary prefix topology, not a ripple chain.

options.text: It is unchanged because each full adder is unchanged
options.explanation: The number of stages on the dependent path has changed.

workedExample: Each stage may need the preceding stage's carry. Doubling the chain therefore doubles its worst-case stage count under the uniform model. A particular input may generate or kill a carry partway through, but timing must allow the longest permitted route.
